# v3.0.0

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **Settings now load from `config.yml`.** `settings.ini` is no longer read.
  Before you upgrade, move your settings from `settings.ini` to `config.yml`.
  Otherwise your existing configuration will be silently ignored. (52569f9)

## Features

- Load settings from `config.yml`. (52569f9)

## Bug fixes

- Retry failed uploads. (a071847)

## Performance

- Cache parsed templates. (4028345)

I wrote the release notes to `RELEASE_NOTES.md`, covering the four commits since the last tag, `v2.3.1`. I haven't committed the file or created a tag.

**I've headed the release v3.0.0, not 2.4.0, because it contains a breaking change.** Commit `52569f9` stops reading `settings.ini`, and settings now come from `config.yml`. Anyone upgrading has to move their settings first, or their existing configuration won't be used. That warning is at the top of the notes.

What's in the notes:

| Section | Change | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| ⚠️ Breaking changes | `settings.ini` is no longer read; move settings to `config.yml` | `52569f9` |
| Features | Settings load from `config.yml` | `52569f9` |
| Bug fixes | Failed uploads are retried | `a071847` |
| Performance | Parsed templates are cached | `4028345` |

I left out the formatting-only commit (`00b8183`, "format with ruff") because users won't notice any change from it.

The repo's only file is `history.txt`, so all of this comes from the commit messages and the breaking-change note in `52569f9`. If you want more detail, such as a sample `config.yml` or how a missing config is handled, tell me where the settings code lives and I'll add it.
